Annual Meetings

Afternoon Session - 2017 Meeting

Warren Buffett defends 3G Capital's efforts to make Kraft Heinz more efficient. He and Charlie Munger also speculate about how the growth of artificial intelligence could affect Berkshire in the future.

Sat, May 6 2017 • 1:00 PM EDT
Key Chapters —
  1. 1. Berkshire and 3G's different approaches to job cuts
  2. 7. Defending 3G's job cuts
  3. 15. I "underestimated the brilliance" of Jeff Bezos at Amazon
  4. 16. "If I died tonight, I think the stock would go up tomorrow."
  5. 23. "We're getting too much medicine"
  6. 27. "Don't wait till you're 93"
1. Berkshire and 3G's different approaches to job cuts

WARREN BUFFETT: Now, the, essentially, 3G management â and I've watched them up very close at Kraft Heinz â is â basically, they don't â they believe in having a company as productive as possible.

Sync Video to Paragraph

If there had been no change in productivity, we would be living the same life as people lived in 1776.

Sync Video to Paragraph

Now, the people â the 3G people â do it very fast. And they're very good at making a business productive with fewer people than operated before.

Sync Video to Paragraph

But that â they've been, you know, we've been doing that in every industry, whether it's steel, or cars, or you name it. And that's why we live as well as we do.

Sync Video to Paragraph
